A_schema.authority: KINE-ADL BE-UJI DATASET_Guide.pdf, KINEMATIC_DATA -> ANGLES block (SHA-256 equals the Mendeley-published hash)
A_schema.hands: BOTH: 18 R_ columns then 18 L_ columns, 36 in total
A_schema.handedness_handling: explicit in the column names; the guide also carries SUBJECT_DATA.LATERALITY (1 = right handed, 2 = left handed)
A_schema.note: 8 of 18 positions differ from the KIN-MUS order, so a positional mapping between the two releases would silently swap four adjacent pairs.

B_subjects.key: (EXPERIMENT, SUBJECT) - the two experiments use their own subject numbering
B_subjects.why_not: which 15 of the 40 (experiment, subject) keys are the same people is stored only in SUBJECT_DATA inside BE_UJI_DATASET.mat (644 185 378 B), which was not downloaded
B_subjects.hazard: a grouped split by SUBJECT that crosses the two experiments leaks 15 people into both folds while looking correct; a split by RECORD range or by EXPERIMENT is safe

C_calibration.units: degrees; 'Joint angles (deg)' in the guide data-structure header [DOC]
C_calibration.reference_posture: hands resting flat on the table, fingers and thumb close together, middle fingers aligned with the forearms; the angle is measured WITH RESPECT TO that posture [DOC]
C_calibration.zero_definition: the recorded reference posture of the session - same convention as KIN-MUS and the MOVMUS guide
C_calibration.positive_direction: PIP(2-5)_F, IP1_F, CMC1_F, MCP(1-5)_F, WR_F: flexion +; MCP(2-3,3-4,4-5)_A: separated +; PalmArch: flexion +; CMC1_F: flexion +; CMC1_A: abduction +; WR_A: ULNAR + / radial - [DOC]
C_calibration.wr_a_vs_kin_mus: OPPOSITE. The KIN-MUS paper says radial + / ulnar -. DOCUMENTATION_CONFLICT across the UJI family.
C_calibration.gloves: CyberGlove II on the RIGHT hand and CyberGlove III on the LEFT hand, 18 strain gauges each [DOC]
C_calibration.instrument_specific_gains: the official code record states plainly that 'gains in the gains_identification.m function have to be replaced with the gains obtained' for one's own glove, and ships the UJI group's gains as placeholders. The gains actually used to build KINE-ADL are NOT published. [DOC]
C_calibration.per_side_gains: the code carries SEPARATE right and left gain vectors of 42 entries each (5 PIP, 5 MCP_f, 18 MCP_a, 1 CMC5, 4 CMC1, 5 WRIST, 4 DIP), so the two gloves are calibrated independently - a shared gain table must never be assumed [DOC]
C_calibration.missing_wrist_angles: the guide marks WR_F and WR_A with '*Some wrist angles are missing because of improper fitting of the wrist sensors to some subjects' hands.' [DOC]
C_calibration.subject_arom_available: yes - SUBJECT_DATA carries per-DOF max/min AROM for both hands, so an AROM-based sanity check is possible once the corpus is obtained [DOC]

D_segmentation.records: RECORD 101..199 (A) and 201..279 (B); a record is one continuous task performed in a natural, non-directed way
D_segmentation.elementary_tasks: every record is divided into ELEMENTARY TASKS, 178 in total (99 in A, 79 in B); each elementary task has its own ID [DOC]
D_segmentation.boundary_definition: the paper: 'the start and the end of each elementary task were identified ... In all other cases, the release was performed on the surface closest to the subject' - the boundary is the object RELEASE / placement event, per the video review [DOC]
D_segmentation.sampling: 100 Hz, filtered with a 2nd-order two-way low-pass Butterworth at 10 Hz [DOC]
D_segmentation.labels_are: trial-wise continuous segments, not frame-wise annotations of an instantaneous class
D_segmentation.api_appendix: the guide's Appendix II lists, per record, the elementary-task ID, the object IDs and the scenario ID, so task content is reconstructible without the corpus

E_observability.method: documentation-based semantic classification only; no kinematic trajectory was available, so nothing here is an observability measurement

1_likely_pose_observable: tasks whose whole content is a hand posture/shape change with no object identity needed, e.g. 'Folding a piece of paper' (A17) start vs end, 'Beating the egg with a fork' (116) vs 'Cleaning the worktop' (210) - wrist oscillation vs flat-hand drag
2_pose_plus_temporal_potentially_observa: repeated cyclic actions: 'Beating the egg with a fork' (116), 'Washing the glass, the bowl, the dish, the fork and the knife' (208), 'Beating an egg and salting it' (130), 'Pouring water from the jug into the cup' (A22/122)
3_object_or_context_dependent: 'Using a toaster' (101), 'Opening the fridge', 'Opening a carton of milk with scissors' (120), 'Taking the pan by the handle' - the identity of the task depends on which object is being held
4_clearly_not_pose_sufficient: 'Carrying utensils and ingredients to the worktop' (112-114), 'Putting the tray with 3 kg of food into the oven' (129), 'Carrying the carton of eggs ... back to the fridge' (127) - whole-body transport, the hand pose is incidental
'*****Displacement without manipulation' rows in the appendix
5_uncertain: the remaining majority of the 178; deciding needs the trajectories

candidate_contrasts.contrast: SINGLE-HAND POSTURE: a power-grip segment vs a pinch-grip segment
candidate_contrasts.why_physical: a cylindrical grip and a pinch grip differ in the MCP/PIP flexion pattern and in the thumb placement; that is a pure hand-shape difference
candidate_contrasts.why_not_object_dependent: the contrast is defined on the SHAPE, not on which object produced it

candidate_contrasts.contrast: HANDEDNESS / ROLE ASYMMETRY: bimanual tasks where one hand stabilises and the other manipulates
candidate_contrasts.why_physical: the two hands' pose distributions differ systematically during the same elementary task
candidate_contrasts.why_not_object_dependent: the contrast is defined per hand

candidate_contrasts.contrast: CYCLE-PHASE within a repeated action (fork beating, cloth wiping): contact vs recovery half-cycle
candidate_contrasts.why_physical: a cyclic action has a hand-shape and velocity signature
candidate_contrasts.why_not_object_dependent: the phase is defined by the action itself

E_observability.verdict: CANDIDATE LIST ONLY.  Every candidate is UNVERIFIED because the corpus was not downloaded; no candidate may be treated as selected.
